title: Regenerate MSW mocks from YNAB spec once msw-auto-mock supports OpenAPI 3.1.1
description:
During the ynab 2->4 upgrade (ynab-tdt), the SDK moved to /plans/... endpoints, so src/mocks/handlers.ts had to be updated. The intended path — 'bun run generate:mocks' — FAILED:

  SyntaxError: Unsupported OpenAPI version: 3.1.1. Swagger Parser only supports versions 3.0.0-3.1.0

YNAB's current spec (api.ynab.com/papi/open_api_spec.yaml, v1.86.0) is OpenAPI 3.1.1; msw-auto-mock's bundled @apidevtools/swagger-parser caps at 3.1.0.

WORKAROUND APPLIED: hand-patched src/mocks/handlers.ts (65 path refs /budgets->/plans + the two top-level response keys data.budgets->data.plans, data.budget->data.plan) and the runtime handlers in ynab-client.test.ts. src/mocks/ynab-openapi.yaml was left at the old 1.77.0 (the curl in generate:mocks overwrote it with 1.86.0, then it was restored). So the committed mock spec (1.77.0) is now STALER than the hand-patched handlers.

CONSEQUENCE: mock response bodies are still spec-1.77.0 shaped (missing newer fields like category internal, goal_frequency, until_date). Tests pass because the SDK's FromJSON tolerates missing optional fields, but the mocks have drifted from the real API.

TO FIX (when tooling allows): either wait for msw-auto-mock to support 3.1.1, or down-convert the spec to 3.0.x before generation, or switch mock generators. Then 'bun run generate:mocks' should regenerate handlers.ts + ynab-openapi.yaml cleanly against the current spec.
acceptance_criteria: 'bun run generate:mocks' runs successfully against the current YNAB spec; handlers.ts + ynab-openapi.yaml regenerated with /plans paths and current response shapes; tests pass
close_reason: Done. Unblocked generate:mocks (relabel OpenAPI 3.1.1->3.1.0 for msw-auto-mock's parser; committed spec keeps true 3.1.1). Rewrote as scripts/generate-mocks.ts with the relabel + a decimal_digits post-processing bound. Made the hand-customizations DURABLE: handlers.ts is now purely generated; the 5 write-endpoint echo handlers moved to hand-written src/mocks/handler-overrides.ts composed before the generated handlers in node.ts (MSW first-match). Spec refreshed 1.77.0->1.86.0 and .prettierignore'd. Verified: 253 tests, signal green, generate:mocks idempotent (byte-identical re-run, never touches overrides/node/script).

title: Upgrade to ESLint 10 once jha-config plugins support it
description:
Blocked as of 2026-07-16. Attempted during the dependency modernization and reverted to eslint 9.39.5.

WHAT HAPPENS: ESLint 10.7.0 installs, then crashes on rule load:
  TypeError: Error while loading rule 'typescript-sort-keys/interface': context.getSourceCode is not a function
ESLint 10 removed context.getSourceCode() (deprecated in v9).

WHY IT'S HARD-BLOCKED -- both offenders are ALREADY at their latest versions and neither has an ESLint 10 release:
  - eslint-plugin-typescript-sort-keys@3.3.0 (latest) -> peer: eslint '^7 || ^8' (does not even claim 9)
  - eslint-plugin-import@2.32.0 (latest)              -> peer: eslint through '^9' only
Both arrive via eslint-config-jha-react-node (Justin's own shared config, itself already at its latest tag 0.3.0).

So the upgrade path runs through the shared config: either those plugins ship ESLint 10 support upstream, or the config drops/replaces them. eslint-plugin-typescript-sort-keys looks the least maintained (still declaring ^7||^8) and may need replacing outright.

RELATED: ynab-mcp-deluxe-yt1 (the ESM interop bug in the same shared config).

CURRENT: eslint 9.39.5, lint green.
acceptance_criteria: eslint on 10.x; 'bun run lint' runs clean; either the plugins ship eslint 10 support or eslint-config-jha-react-node drops/replaces them

title: Fix month merge bug: nested categories not merged correctly
description:
Delta sync validation revealed that mergeMonthArray() is not correctly merging months.

**Problem:**
When a delta response includes months, we replace the entire month object instead of merging the nested categories array. This causes drift detection to find 526 differences (83 months, 443 transactions).

**Root cause:**
In mergeMonthArray(), line 179: `byMonth.set(month.month, month)` replaces the entire month.
But MonthDetail contains a nested `categories` array that should be merged, not replaced.

**Evidence from logs:**
```
🚨 DRIFT DETECTED - merge logic produced different result
differenceCount: 526
differenceSummary: { months: 83, transactions: 443 }
```

The differences are all `kind: "N"` (New) items in `months.X.categories[Y]` - categories exist in full fetch but not in merged budget.

**Fix needed:**
When merging a month, need to merge the nested categories array rather than replacing the whole month object.

**Reference:** 
- Scratchpad: docs/plans/2026-01-28_pino-logging-delta-sync-validation.md
- Related to: ynab-mcp-deluxe-b3u (Validate delta sync with real YNAB API)
close_reason: Fixed in 47fcc14 - mergeMonthArray now merges nested categories array instead of replacing

title: Fix ESM interop bug in eslint-config-jha-react-node react entry
description:
The shared config package eslint-config-jha-react-node (v0.3.0) crashes ESLint for any project using its react entry (or the default '.' entry, which includes react).

ROOT CAUSE (verified 2026-07-16):
In dist/cjs/react.cjs:
  var reactRefresh = require('eslint-plugin-react-refresh');   // line 6
  plugins: {'react-refresh': reactRefresh}                      // line 28

eslint-plugin-react-refresh@0.5.2 (the version the config pins) is ESM-transpiled. require() returns the module namespace {__esModule, default, reactRefresh}, so .rules is undefined -- the rules actually live at .default.rules. ESLint cannot resolve 'react-refresh/only-export-components' and throws:

  TypeError: Key "rules": Key "react-refresh/only-export-components": Could not find "only-export-components" in plugin "react-refresh".

Verified via: node -e "const p=require('eslint-plugin-react-refresh'); console.log(Object.keys(p), p.rules, Object.keys(p.default.rules))"
  -> top keys: ['__esModule','default','reactRefresh']; p.rules: undefined; p.default.rules: ['only-export-components']

IMPACT: any React project consuming this config has ESLint fully broken (crash on startup = zero rules running), plus husky pre-commit and CI lint failing. In ynab-mcp-deluxe this went unnoticed for months.

FIX: unwrap the interop in the shared config, e.g.
  const reactRefreshPlugin = reactRefresh.default ?? reactRefresh;
or configure rollup interop:'auto' for that import. Same class of bug may affect the other plugins imported the same way (jsx-a11y, react, react-hooks) if/when they ship ESM -- worth auditing all four.

NOTE: ynab-mcp-deluxe itself is FIXED (PR #20) by switching to the /node entrypoint, which is correct here regardless (Node MCP server, not React). This bead tracks the upstream package fix, which lives in a different repo.
acceptance_criteria: eslint-config-jha-react-node react entry loads without crashing under eslint-plugin-react-refresh@0.5.2; a React project consuming it runs lint successfully; the other plugin imports (jsx-a11y, react, react-hooks) audited for the same interop pattern

title: Upgrade ynab SDK 2.10.0 -> 4.5.0 (own session: changelog review + patch rework)
description:
Deliberately excluded from the 2026-07-16 fleet-wide dependency bump. Justin's call: 'That'll be its own session looking at the changelog.'

WHY IT'S ITS OWN SESSION -- the patch interaction:
We carry patches/ynab@2.10.0.patch (added by PR #17), which null-guards MonthDetail:
  - 'categories': (json['categories'].map(Category_1.CategoryFromJSON)),
  + 'categories': (json['categories'] == null ? [] : json['categories'].map(Category_1.CategoryFromJSON)),
(same for MonthDetailToJSONTyped). Without it, delta-sync responses containing a month with null categories crash the SDK.

bun's patchedDependencies keys on the EXACT version string ('ynab@2.10.0'), so bumping ynab silently orphans the patch. package.json must be updated in lockstep or the crash returns.

FIRST QUESTION FOR THAT SESSION: is the null-categories bug fixed upstream in 3.x/4.x? If yes, DROP the patch entirely (best outcome). If no, re-create it against 4.5.0 via 'bun patch ynab@4.5.0'.

TWO MAJORS TO CROSS (2.x -> 4.x). Read both changelogs -- this SDK is generated from the YNAB OpenAPI spec, so model/enum shapes can shift. Note this project's CRITICAL rule: enums must be sourced from the SDK, never re-typed, so enum changes propagate into our Zod schemas.

VERIFY AFTER: full test suite (253 currently), plus a real delta sync against a live budget with a month that has null categories -- that is the exact case the patch exists for, and mocks will not catch its regression.

Everything else was bumped 2026-07-16 (fastmcp 4, zod 4, TypeScript 7, vitest 4, eslint 10, etc.).
acceptance_criteria: ynab upgraded to 4.5.0 (or latest); the null-categories crash is either fixed upstream (patch dropped) or re-patched against the new version with patchedDependencies updated to match; full test suite passes; a live delta sync over a month with null categories verified not to crash
notes:
SCOUTING COMPLETE (2026-07-17). Findings:
- null-categories bug NOT fixed upstream in v4.5.0 (dist/models/MonthDetail.js still has unguarded json['categories'].map). MUST re-patch.
- v3/v4 breaking change = YNAB 'budgets'->'plans' API rename: BudgetDetail->PlanDetail, BudgetSummary->PlanSummary; api.budgets.getBudgets()->api.plans.getPlans(); api.budgets.getBudgetById()->api.plans.getPlanById(); response .data.budgets->.data.plans, .data.budget->.data.plan. NO backwards-compat aliases (tsc confirms .budgets and BudgetDetail fully removed).
- v4 createAccount now takes SaveAccountType (6 values: checking/savings/cash/creditCard/otherAsset/otherLiability) NOT AccountType (13 values incl debt/loan types). Real behavior change to create_account tool.
- CategoryGroup gained required 'internal' boolean (API v1.84.0). Only affects test fixtures.
- Enums AccountType/TransactionClearedStatus/TransactionFlagColor now const-objects; Object.values() derivation still works, member access still works.
DECISION: alias Plan* types to Budget* to preserve our 'budget' domain vocabulary (MCP tool names, YNAB_BUDGET_ID all say budget). Only adapt at SDK boundary.
close_reason: Done. ynab 2.10.0 -> 4.5.0. v3/v4 budgets->plans rename adapted at SDK boundary (types aliased Plan*->Budget* to keep our domain vocabulary; api.plans.getPlans/getPlanById; .data.plans/.plan). LocalBudget cache switched to *Base entity types (nullable-friendly, matches what the plan detail returns). createAccount now uses SaveAccountType (creatable subset). null-categories bug NOT fixed upstream in 4.5.0 -> patch recreated as patches/ynab@4.5.0.patch (guards CJS+ESM MonthDetail), patchedDependencies updated. MSW handlers hand-patched to /plans (generate:mocks blocked by OpenAPI 3.1.1 -> follow-up bead ynab-0t1). VERIFIED: 253/253 tests, signal green, build OK, AND real-data on v4 -- server boots, 18 tools, get_budgets/get_budget_summary(21 real categories)/query_transactions OK, and a live DELTA sync (last_knowledge_of_server=131 to /plans) returned 7 months without crashing (the exact null-categories crash path).

title: Upgrade to TypeScript 7 once typescript-eslint supports it
description:
Blocked as of 2026-07-16. Attempted during the dependency modernization and reverted to TypeScript 6.0.3.

WHAT HAPPENS: TypeScript 7.0.2 installs fine and 'tsc --noEmit' actually PASSES clean on this codebase. The blocker is purely lint:

  TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'Cjs')
    at @typescript-eslint/typescript-estree/dist/create-program/shared.js:59
    (exports.DEFAULT_EXTRA_FILE_EXTENSIONS = new Set([ts.Extension.Cjs, ...]))

TS7 is the native Go rewrite (tsgo) and no longer exposes the internal Extension enum that typescript-estree reads at module load.

WHY IT'S HARD-BLOCKED: typescript-eslint@8.64.0 -- the LATEST -- declares
  peerDependencies: { typescript: '>=4.8.4 <6.1.0' }
So this isn't a version-pinning accident; typescript-eslint simply does not support TS7 yet. Running TS7 would mean NO linting at all, which is precisely the state this repo was accidentally in for months before 2026-07-16.

CURRENT: typescript 6.0.3 (stable, released, inside the supported range). Still a real major bump from 5.9.3.

WHEN TO REVISIT: watch for a typescript-eslint release widening the peer range past <6.1.0 / declaring TS7 support. Then bump typescript to 7.x and verify 'bun run lint' still runs.
acceptance_criteria: typescript on 7.x; 'bun run lint' runs without crashing; 'bun run signal' green; 253+ tests pass
